mcqs.q: Periodontal examination consists of:
opts: Careful visual evaluation of the gingiva PLUS careful probing
mcqs.explain: It combines visual evaluation of the gingival margin (biofilm, calculus, inflammation) with careful probing of the gingiva, crevice and subgingival surface.

mcqs.q: Before the gingiva can be reliably observed it must first be:
mcqs.explain: The gingiva is dried before inspection; otherwise stippling and surface texture cannot be judged accurately.

mcqs.q: The color of healthy gingiva is described as:
mcqs.explain: Healthy gingiva is coral or salmon pink; inflammation makes it erythematous or cyanotic.

mcqs.q: Which consistency is typical of INFLAMED gingiva?
mcqs.explain: Inflamed gingiva is soft, edematous and spongy due to collagen breakdown and fluid influx; firmness implies health or fibrosis.

mcqs.q: A knife-edge margin with scalloped architecture and pointed interdental papillae indicates:
mcqs.explain: Thin, knife-edge margins and pointed papillae are signs of health; inflammation gives rolled margins and bulbous papillae.

mcqs.q: Stippling (an orange-peel surface) is a sign of:
mcqs.explain: Stippling reflects healthy connective-tissue attachment; with inflammation the surface becomes smooth and shiny.

mcqs.q: A smooth, shiny gingival surface with loss of stippling suggests:
mcqs.explain: Loss of stippling → smooth, shiny surface is a feature of inflammatory disease.

mcqs.q: The earliest clinical sign of gingival inflammation is:
mcqs.explain: BOP precedes visible color change and is the earliest objective sign of inflammation.

mcqs.q: After probing, bleeding should be rechecked at:
mcqs.explain: Bleeding may be delayed, so the site is re-checked 30–60 seconds after probing.

mcqs.q: For a bleeding index, each tooth is probed at how many sites?
mcqs.explain: Six sites per tooth: mesial, mid and distal on both buccal and lingual surfaces.

mcqs.q: The total number of sites in a full-mouth bleeding index equals:
mcqs.explain: Total sites = teeth present × 6 (six sites per tooth).

mcqs.q: The bleeding score is calculated as:
mcqs.explain: Bleeding score = number of bleeding sites × 100 ÷ total number of sites.

mcqs.q: Long-standing chronic inflammation tends to make the gingiva:
mcqs.explain: Chronic inflammation can be fibrotic — firm, leathery consistency from fibrosis and epithelial proliferation.

mcqs.q: Pitting of the gingiva on pressure is associated with:
mcqs.explain: Pitting on pressure indicates edematous, diseased tissue; a blanched appearance is normal.

mcqs.q: Normally the gingival margin lies on enamel, relative to the CEJ, about:
mcqs.explain: The healthy gingival margin sits roughly 1.5–2 mm coronal to the cemento-enamel junction.

mcqs.q: Gingival recession is defined as:
opts: Exposure of root surface by apical shift of the marginal gingiva
mcqs.explain: Recession = apical migration of the gingival margin exposing the root surface.

mcqs.q: On the chart, GMP is recorded as (+) when the gingival margin is:
opts: At the level of the CEJ
mcqs.explain: (+) = margin apical to CEJ (recession); (0) = at the CEJ; (−) = coronal to / covering the CEJ.

mcqs.q: A GMP notation of (−) means the free gingival margin:
mcqs.explain: (−) indicates the margin is coronal to and covers the CEJ; (+) is apical.

mcqs.q: Which is a recognised feature of a mucogingival deformity?
mcqs.explain: Mucogingival problems include pockets/recession beyond the MGJ, shallow vestibule, high frenal attachment and inadequate attached gingiva.

mcqs.q: The full-mouth periodontal examination should START in the:
mcqs.explain: Begin in the molar region of either arch and proceed systematically around the arch.

mcqs.q: A periodontal pocket is best defined as:
mcqs.explain: A pocket is a pathologically deepened gingival sulcus, detected by probing.

mcqs.q: A suprabony pocket is one in which the base of the pocket is:
opts: Coronal to the alveolar bone crest
Apical to the alveolar bone crest
mcqs.explain: Suprabony = pocket base coronal to bone; intrabony = base apical to the bone crest.

mcqs.q: An intrabony (infrabony) pocket has its base:
opts: Apical to the crest of the alveolar bone
mcqs.explain: In an intrabony pocket the base lies apical to the alveolar crest, beside the root.

mcqs.q: The recommended probing force is approximately:
mcqs.explain: A probing force of about 25 g is used; excessive force gives falsely deep readings.

mcqs.q: During probing the probe should be directed:
opts: Parallel to the long axis of the tooth
mcqs.explain: Keep the probe parallel to the long axis (angled only obliquely to detect interproximal craters).

mcqs.q: “Walking” the probe means:
opts: Moving it circumferentially around the pocket in small steps
mcqs.explain: The probe is walked in small steps circumferentially to map the whole pocket.

mcqs.q: Clinical attachment loss is measured from the:
opts: CEJ to the bottom of the probeable crevice
mcqs.explain: CAL = distance from the CEJ (fixed landmark) to the base of the probeable crevice.

mcqs.q: When the gingival margin is APICAL to the CEJ, the CAL equals:
mcqs.explain: With recession, CAL = probing depth + the amount of recession (gingival margin–to–CEJ distance).

mcqs.q: On the Miller mobility index, movement of the crown up to 1 mm in any direction is:
mcqs.explain: Grade 1 = first movement beyond normal; Grade 2 = up to 1 mm; Grade 3 = >1 mm or vertical/rotational movement.

mcqs.q: Furcation areas of multirooted teeth are best examined with a:
mcqs.explain: A curved Nabers probe is designed to enter and grade furcation involvement.

mcqs.q: This image shows a completed clinical record. What is it?
mcqs.explain: It is a periodontal charting form recording probing depths, gingival margin position and CAL for six sites per tooth.

mcqs.q: Identify the instrument being used in this image.
mcqs.explain: The curved Nabers probe is entering the furcation of multirooted teeth to assess furcation involvement.

mcqs.q: A patient is identified as a periodontitis case when:
opts: Interproximal CAL is detectable at ≥2 non-adjacent teeth
Any single site bleeds on probing
mcqs.explain: 2017 case definition: interproximal CAL at ≥2 non-adjacent teeth, OR buccal/lingual CAL ≥3 mm with pocketing at ≥2 teeth.

saqs.q: Define bleeding on probing (BOP) and state when it should be rechecked.
saqs.a: BOP = bleeding from the pocket wall after gentle probing — the earliest sign of gingival inflammation. Recheck 30–60 seconds after probing.

saqs.q: List the clinical characteristics assessed when examining the gingiva.
saqs.a: Color, size, contour, consistency, surface texture, position, ease of bleeding, and pain.

saqs.q: Contrast healthy and inflamed gingiva for color, consistency and surface texture.
A site has a 4 mm probing depth and the gingival margin is 2 mm apical to the CEJ. What is the CAL?
saqs.a: CAL = probing depth + recession = 4 + 2 = 6 mm of attachment loss.

saqs.q: State the bleeding-score formula and how the total number of sites is obtained.
saqs.a: Bleeding score = (bleeding sites × 100) ÷ total sites; total sites = number of teeth × 6.

saqs.q: Interproximal CAL is found at the upper-right central incisor and the lower-left first molar. Is this periodontitis?
saqs.a: Yes — interproximal CAL at ≥2 non-adjacent teeth meets the 2017 case definition of periodontitis.
